subject: The bed has to work for the person helping at 2am
preheader: Complex overnight support is a whole-room problem, not only a mattress question.
intro: For a child or young person with complex physical support needs, the bed decision affects more than comfort.
It has to work for positioning, transfers, care routines, the people providing assistance and the other equipment already in the room.
body: A mattress may feel appropriate while the bed height makes a transfer harder. A side or accessory may help one task and obstruct another. The support person may not have the access they need once everything is in the room.
A useful home trial brings the person, support routine, room and equipment together before the final decision.
questions: Can the person be positioned and repositioned as intended?
Can family or support workers provide assistance from the space available?
Do the bed, mattress and transfer equipment work together?
What needs to change before the OT recommends the next step?
actionText: Tell us about the person's needs and goals, their overnight support routine, the room and the equipment already being used. We'll help work out what should be trialled together and whether an in-home trial is practical.
teamName: The Sleep Choice x Supply Ministry Team
trialFooterText: Seven-night in-home trial availability, service area, equipment configuration and individual arrangements are confirmed per case.
